beats.narration_text: Hello. I'm Kalyan Karnati, and this is the pitch for my final project. The usual question is which health-tech companies sponsor visas. For an early-career product manager, the real question is which ones sponsor product managers.

show.event: backspaces 'sponsor visas' → 'sponsor product managers' on the spoken correction

beats.motion_claim: The writer types the usual visa question and corrects it to the real one: sponsoring product managers.

qc.sparse_reason: Hesitant-writer bookend: the correction is the motion.

beats.narration_text: An H-1B sponsor is an employer that files work-visa petitions. A SOC code is the government's job category for a role. A liveness check asks whether a job posting is still open.

terms.meaning: an employer that files work-visa petitions
the government's job category for a role
asks whether a job posting is still open

qc.sparse_reason: TERMS card: three prerequisites, one line each.

beats.narration_text: I'm building PM Sponsor Check: a tool that tells an early-career product manager which health-tech employers have public evidence of sponsoring product managers, not just engineers, and labels every answer as a record or a guess.

shot.visual_intent: The open kraft box drops onto the floor; a scan block, an evidence page and a record-or-guess tray drop into it. Labelled 'constructed'.
shot.motion_claim: The open kraft box drops onto the floor; a scan block, an evidence page and a record-or-guess tray drop into it. Labelled 'constructed'.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, with the voice carrying the explanation. The negative space is the style, so only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: It matters because the usual check misleads. On my first run, only nine of three hundred fifty-two possible health sponsors listed a product manager title among their top sponsored roles, and none of those titles was entry level.

shot.visual_intent: 352 crate tops in rows; a scan line sweeps; nine light up; the hero number '9 of 352' lands.
shot.motion_claim: 352 crate tops in rows; a scan line sweeps; nine light up; the hero number '9 of 352' lands.

beats.narration_text: Two public tools already exist. The government's H-1B Employer Data Hub counts petitions by company, industry and year, but not by job title, so it can't tell me who sponsors product managers.

shot.visual_intent: Two ink windows, 'Data Hub' and 'MyVisaJobs'. Data Hub grows company, industry and year columns; an empty dashed slot appears where a job-title column would be.
shot.motion_claim: Two ink windows, 'Data Hub' and 'MyVisaJobs'. Data Hub grows company, industry and year columns; an empty dashed slot appears where a job-title column would be.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, with the voice carrying the explanation. The negative space is the style, so only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: MyVisaJobs goes further: I can search by job title and see wage levels. What neither does is check whether a posting is still open, or label which answers are records and which are guesses. That's what mine adds.

shot.visual_intent: Continues from I1A: MyVisaJobs grows title rows and wage bars; both windows get an empty dashed lamp; a third window, 'mine', arrives with a live card, a terracotta lamp and a check, labelled 'constructed'.
shot.motion_claim: Continues from I1A: MyVisaJobs grows title rows and wage bars; both windows get an empty dashed lamp; a third window, 'mine', arrives with a live card, a terracotta lamp and a check, labelled 'constructed'.

beats.narration_text: The Reallocation Engine I'm building on rates each company's sponsorship as one tier, like "Likely," for the whole company, not for a role.

shot.visual_intent: Two windows: the engine scorer's row grows one tier bar; my row grows the same bar plus a separate PM chip with a check.
shot.motion_claim: Two windows: the engine scorer's row grows one tier bar; my row grows the same bar plus a separate PM chip with a check.

beats.narration_text: Job boards keep stale copies: on my second run, Built In Boston still listed copies of Cohere Health roles marked removed, while the live role sat on Cohere's own board.

shot.visual_intent: Left window 'Built In': job cards greyed with a cross. Right, the company's own board: one live card; a check lands.
shot.motion_claim: Left window 'Built In': job cards greyed with a cross. Right, the company's own board: one live card; a check lands.

beats.narration_text: And filtering by health industry would have quietly dropped sixty-four sponsors filed under technology and other categories. That's why mine is worth building: it checks the role, not just the company.

beats.narration_text: The data is public. I start from the repository's 80 Days to Stay table, which joins SEC Form D filings, which report funding, with H-1B records from the Labor Department and U S C I S, for about thirty thousand companies.

shot.visual_intent: A wide grid of crates slides through an ink gate; a small stack lands on the other side.
shot.motion_claim: A wide grid of crates slides through an ink gate; a small stack lands on the other side.

beats.narration_text: Step one, the health industry category and a keyword filter find possible health companies. Step two, a scan reads each one's sponsored job titles for product roles. Step three, a liveness check confirms the posting is still open before anything gets an Apply.

shot.visual_intent: One conveyor with three gates, numbered 1 to 3 in ink: filter, title scan, liveness. A crate rides through each gate in turn; after gate 3 an 'Apply' pill and a check land. Gate 3 is labelled 'constructed'.
shot.motion_claim: One conveyor with three gates, numbered 1 to 3 in ink: filter, title scan, liveness. A crate rides through each gate in turn; after gate 3 an 'Apply' pill and a check land. Gate 3 is labelled 'constructed'.

beats.narration_text: Step four will add the full Labor Department filing data, the only way to confirm product-manager sponsorship beyond a top-titles list. It's large and messy, so I'll start with one fiscal year, the most recent complete one, and say so in the log.

shot.visual_intent: A tall messy stack of filing pages wobbles; a thin slice slides off to the right, labelled '1 year', 'constructed'.

beats.narration_text: What I have: the public data, the scripts, and a free local pipeline. What's tight: an eight-gigabyte laptop, which already forced me to render this film at ten-eighty p, and AI usage limits, which I hit once while I was setting up the engine.

shot.visual_intent: A small desk: a data page, a key and a laptop land on it; then the laptop's memory bar fills and a usage gauge fills to its end.
shot.motion_claim: A small desk: a data page, a key and a laptop land on it; then the laptop's memory bar fills and a usage gauge fills to its end.

beats.narration_text: It will not say which job code an employer will file, and it will not give immigration advice.

beats.narration_text: First, precision. I hand-checked sixty-four keyword matches; today the filter gets fifty-two right, eighty-one percent. It works if the tightened filter beats that on the same sixty-four, measured by one logged command. My target is at least fifty-eight of sixty-four.

shot.visual_intent: The gauge from B08: it fills to 52 / 64; a dashed target mark drops in at 58 / 64, labelled 'constructed'.
shot.motion_claim: The gauge from B08: it fills to 52 / 64; a dashed target mark drops in at 58 / 64, labelled 'constructed'.

beats.narration_text: Second, honesty of the ranking. On my first run the scorer marked unchecked postings as checked. It works if no unchecked posting ever ranks above a checked one, and the log proves it.

shot.visual_intent: A two-row ranking: the unchecked card sits on top with a false grey check; a scan line sweeps it and the false check is struck.
shot.motion_claim: A two-row ranking: the unchecked card sits on top with a false grey check; a scan line sweeps it and the false check is struck.

beats.narration_text: It didn't work if any Apply goes out without a liveness check, or if a company is called a PM sponsor without a filing record behind it. Either one counts as a failure, logged, not hidden.

shot.visual_intent: A run-log page: a pass row with a check, then a fail row with a cross; a terracotta dot marks the logged failure.
